data.narrative:
Viam, a Series C robotics and manufacturing software company, is valued against a universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable across the robotics sector. The peer set includes established ventures like Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), and Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), alongside earlier-stage competitors.

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses Viam's $117M total raised as a proxy base, applying a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C-to-next-stage transitions, yielding $199M. The peer-median method draws from 7 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables, producing a $1.6B median valuation with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B. The wide dispersion reflects stage and business model variance within the peer cohort—notably, several peers occupy Series B and Series D positions, creating measurement noise around a pure Series C benchmark.

Triangulation across both methods implies a valuation range of $169M to $1.9B, with a median of $924M. The stage-progression method suggests floor-level defensibility; the peer-median implies substantial upside conditional on Viam's growth trajectory and competitive positioning. Key uncertainties include revenue scale relative to peers, capital efficiency post-Series C, and the company's path to sustainable unit economics in manufacturing automation.
